newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan cement firm share offer oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan cement firm share offer oversubscribed.

text.p: A share offer by Kenya's Athi River Mining that ended on Wednesday was oversubcribed despite a slow start under difficult conditions of political unrest, brokers said.
"The issue managers have received hundreds of applications in the past two days which are still being processed and reconciled," a statement by the company said.

The total offer consisted of 23 million shares worth 281.75 million shillings ($4.9 million). More than 15.7 million shares were offered to the public at 12.25 shillings (20 cents) each, of which 70 percent were reserved for institutional investors.

The company's investment advisers said they could not provide a final figure for the offer, which began on July 10, because they were yet to receive applications from areas outside the capital but projected an oversubscription rate of 30 percent.
"My guess is about 350 million shillings have been raised which is definitely above what were looking for," a sponsoring broker said.
Athi River is the second initial public offering in Kenya this year after Tourism Promotion Services, the trading name of leading hotel concern Serena Lodges and Hotels Ltd.
The Athi River offering was a difficult one because it occurred against a background of some of the worst political unrest the country has known since July 1990, brokers said.
"The investment climate was not positive. But local investors did come through, especially retail," Amish Gupta of leading brokerage house Shah, Munge & Partners said.

Nine people were killed in violent clashes between police protestors calling for constitutional reforms on July 7. The violent protests worried investors and the Nairobi Stock Exchange sank to an all-year low on that date and has not yet recovered -- mostly because many foreign investors stopped buying or cancelled or suspended orders.
Brokers said they also had difficulty convincing medium-term investors, which are the majority in the Kenyan market but buy for quick short-term gains.
Athi River's announcement that it would use 40 percent of the funds raised from the offer to offset an outstanding loan cast a shadow on the offer and dampened speculator interest.

Cement production is the company's core business and accounts for 60 percent of turnover while industrial minerals and chemicals account for 19 and 21 percent respectively. The firm averages 5,500 tonnes of cement a month and has five percent of the Kenyan cement market. Some 140 million shillings raised from the offer will go to expanding the plant's capacity and increase production to 108,000 tonnes per year.
Athi River posted after-tax profits in 1996 at 28.147 million shillings from 18.78 million in 1995. It has forecast after-tax profits to reach 46.2 million shillings in 1997.
The firm will be the third cement company quoted on the NSE after Bamburi Cement and East African Portland Cement and the 58th listed company on the bourse.
The basis of the share allotment is to be released on July 30.
